label: refusal re-audit — pra-05-01 recovered via signChart, an engine never checked when it was refused

widget.prompt: (x − 3)/(x + 1) has TWO kinds of cut: a zero, where the function genuinely reaches 0, and an excluded value, where it is undefined. Place both, then mark the sign on each interval.
widget.successFeedback: Positive, negative, positive — and the two cuts are not the same kind of thing. x = 3 sits ON the axis: the numerator is zero there, so the function is genuinely 0. x = −1 is the dashed line: the denominator is zero, so the function is undefined and the sign flips ACROSS a value it never takes. Both cut the chart; only one is a solution.
widget.crossFeedback: A sign was missed across an odd-multiplicity cut. Both x = 3 and x = −1 have multiplicity 1, so the sign flips at each one.
widget.bounceFeedback: A sign was flipped where it should have held, or held where it should have flipped — check each cut's multiplicity before deciding whether the sign changes there.

refusals.title: Rational root candidates, synthetic division, FTA zero-counting, conjugate pairs, building from mixed zeros, slant division
refusals.why: RE-CONFIRMED in S203Y after pra-05-01 (originally refused in the SAME bulk group) turned out to be recoverable. Each of these six was re-read individually against signChart, the engine that rescued pra-05-01: listing divisors of a constant, running a synthetic-division tableau, counting zeros by the Fundamental Theorem, applying the Conjugate Root Theorem, computing a sum/product of complex roots, and polynomial long division. signChart models the SIGN of a factored expression across its cuts — it has no representation for a division tableau, a candidate list, or a multiplicity count as a computed answer. These six are genuinely symbolic procedures and the refusals stand, now on a checked basis rather than a bulk one.
